title: Fixed Divergent Tapes and Three Mouth Slider Fastener
description: One wholly newly authored complete partially open zipper-style connector, laid flat in one fixed display pose. Two continuous finite-thickness textile-looking tapes run from near-parallel lower sections into divergent upper ends. Whole blunt headed teeth alternate along the lower centre and form separate upper rows; a complete bottom stop and two complete upper stops belong to the same assembly. At the split, separate full lower/upper plates, two tapered side rails and one whole triangular divider enclose a real two-entrance/one-exit slider-shaped chamber. A continuous raised bridge carries a full inclined pull tab with a genuine long through window. This is not the old pair of thick rigid comb plates with a constant meandering interface, nor a two-mount lever draw latch and keeper. Every visible coordinate is new; no old clothing, fastener or tooth meshes imported, and tooth count/colour does not establish novelty. One complete connector prop, zero scenes, four opaque constant untextured PBR appearances, metre-style native Z up, whole horizontal envelope centred on the tapes and lower-plate ground datum. Enlarged simplified artistic object, not a manufacturing or repair diagram. Fixed joins and deliberate sparse gaps are not working tooth engagement or a validated slider route. No host garment, stitching, cloth deformation, flexibility, opening/closing, slider travel, fastening strength, load, hand fit, protective equipment use, manufacture, installation or safety capability is made or verified. Rigging animation and interaction not made.
